newsitem.title: USA: Apache extends Egypt's North Qarun Field.
newsitem.headline: Apache extends Egypt's North Qarun Field.

text.p: Apache Corp said Wednesday it has completed the North Qarun 4-X step-out oil producer, extending the limits of North Qarun field in Egypt's Western Desert.
Results of this well, combined with 3-D seismic and additional geologic interpretations, indicate the North Qarun field may be larger than previously estimated, Apache said.
The company said it plans to drill additional appraisal wells to further define the field and also will drill an exploratory well to the north to test a look-alike structure.
The 75 percent owned field, formerly the Qarun "B" field, is one of three Apache oil fields on the northern part of the Qarun Concession. Seagull Energy Corp has the remaining 25 percent interest.

The 4-X well is flowing into pipeline at the rate of 1,950 barrels of 39-degree gravity crude oil through a 36/64-inch choke with a flowing tubing pressure of 320 pounds per square inch. It is producing from 142 feet of pay in the Lower Bahariya formation perforated at about 8,700 feet.
Apache said this is the thickest pay section encountered to date in North Qarun field.

The new producer brings to 25 the number of oil wells that Apache has completed of 28 wells drilled in the three-field Qarun area since 1995. Production from a fourth Qarun field located on the southern part of the concession, the Wadi El Rayan, will be trucked to market beginning next week.

The company said it has 13 drilling rigs running in the Western Desert, including six on the Qarun Concession, and expects to drill a total of 62 wells in Egypt during 1997. Two-thirds of these wells are exploratory.
Apache and Seagull are 50-50 contractor partners in two other Egyptian concessions: East Beni Suef and Darag.
